subject: Bridging capacity gap — renewal health, token variance & sprint for term change
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumentech.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridging capacity gap — renewal health, token variance & sprint for term change

Hi Aisha,

Quick summary from our side ahead of the renewal conversation next month. We reviewed LumenTech's Q1 token usage and performance profile and want to call out three items that matter for the term conversation:

1) Token variance: weekly peak usage increased ~42% vs baseline (primarily inference burst windows for your doc-processing jobs). The rolling average is up ~18%.
2) Latency profile: 95th pct latency on the main embedding route crept from 220ms to ~290ms during spikes — appears correlated with large batched runs.
3) Cost/ROI: your current reserved commit covers ~74% of off-peak traffic; uncovered bursts are hitting on-demand tokens and driving unit cost up ~28% month-over-month.

Attachments: I included a CSV with weekly breakdown and a draft SLA addendum that shows how a modest commit uplift plus a small burst pool would change your expected unit economics.

Proposal / asks:
- Short term (term change): increase committed capacity by 25% for the 12-month renewal with a 6% blended discount; add an automatic burst lane of 80k tokens/day for scheduled batch runs.
- Operational sprint: coordinate a two-week pre-renewal runbook to test batching/kv-cache hints we recommend (we'll provide runner scripts).
- Call: can we lock a 30-minute slot next week to walk through the CSV and the SLA draft? Ideally include someone from procurement.

If you prefer, we can instead package the uplift as a staged addendum (6 months bridge + final term) — happy to discuss tradeoffs.

Thanks,

Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: LumenTech_usage_Q1.csv (csv, 42 KB stub), SLA_draft_3.docx (docx, 68 KB stub)

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumentech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridging capacity gap — renewal health, token variance & sprint for term change

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the concise summary. A few clarifying questions before we pull procurement in: 

- Can you break down the ~42% peak increase by feature? Is this concentrated to the nightly doc pipeline or multiple services?
- The proposed 25% uplift — what does that translate to in committed tokens/month and expected cost delta?
- Can you provide a short ROI note showing expected net unit-cost change if we adopt the uplift + burst lane?

Procurement will want numbers we can feed into our renewal model. We have an internal budget freeze window the week of 3/20, so would prefer the sprint/testing to happen before then.

I can take a 30-min slot on Wed 3/14 after 1pm PT. Monica will loop in our procurement lead if the numbers check out.

Best,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Engineering
LumenTech
aisha.khan@lumentech.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumentech.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridging capacity gap — renewal health, token variance & sprint for term change

Nice — thanks Aisha. Quick answers inline and attached a one-page ROI snapshot.

- Peak breakdown: ~78% of the peak delta is your nightly doc-processing pipeline (the multi-file batch jobs that hit embeddings + long-context summarization). The remaining 22% is smaller, ad-hoc conversational and search workloads during business hours.
- Committed tokens: a 25% uplift equals ~4.5M committed tokens/mo (from current 18M to 22.5M). Estimated incremental spend before discount: ~$36k/mo.
- Net unit-cost delta: with our proposed 6% blended discount + burst lane (which moves bursts to a cheaper reserved-backed lane) we model a ~14% reduction in your blended per-token cost compared to current on-demand heavy months. ROI PDF attached (1 page).

Operational notes: we recommend the two-week sprint focus on:
- Prefetch & KV-cache hints for the nightly pipeline to reduce duplicate context tokens
- Reducing batch sizes during business-hour windows to smooth 95th pct latency

I'm available Wed 3/14 at 1:30pm PT — tentatively blocked that slot. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda and the runbook tasks.

Regards,

Marcus
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: LumenTech_Q1_ROI_onepager.pdf (pdf, 24 KB stub)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@lumentech.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridging capacity gap — renewal health, token variance & sprint for term change

Thanks both — looping in a quick operational checklist before the Wed call so LumenTech's engineers have a clear path: 

1) We will supply a small runner that collects cache-hit rates across the nightly jobs (script + README).
2) We'll propose prefetch keys for the top 10 templates we see in your corpus.
3) Ops validation: a short A/B during the sprint (one week with prefetch, one week baseline) so we can quantify latency + token delta.

Action items: Marcus to send calendar invite for Wed 3/14 1:30pm PT (confirmed). Marcus/Monica to drop the CSV + ROI one-pager into the shared drive link before EOD. Aisha — if procurement can join the call, we'll surface a clean commit option and an addendum template the same day.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
